The Pentagon has confirmed that a third American aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports the last time three carrier strike groups assembled was at the start
of the war with Iran.
U.S. Central Command posted on social media that the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group
has arrived in the Middle East as part of what it calls a scheduled deployment.
The buildup of American firepower is a contrast to recent comments by President Trump that the
war is effectively over. Major combat operations stop during the summer, leaving a stalemate.
The U.S. continues to blockade Iranian ports, and Iran still controls the Strait of Hormuz,
which has driven up prices of petroleum products worldwide.
Iran is likely to be a topic when President Trump meets with the leaders of China and Russia this
week. Russia's Vladimir Putin has openly supported Iran in the conflict.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
Commercial air traffic is just about back to normal. Three days after a communications meltdown
that led the FAA to ground planes from taking off across the country, the Trump administration is
trying to use the moment to lobby for tens of billions of dollars to upgrade the country's
air traffic control infrastructure. But as NPR's Sam Greenglass reports, Democrats say
Congress has already funded the improvements.
Democrats say of that money, some $9 billion remains unspent. Congresswoman Rosa Deloro,
who is the top Democrat on the Appropriations Committee in the House, said in a statement that
Cabinet heads need to take responsibility for mismanagement of funds. A handful of lawmakers
have also said the administration, if they need more money, they should divert some of
the billions of dollars Republicans have already allocated to ICE last year with few strings
attached. NPR's Sam Greenglass reporting, across the U.S., large data centers are driving enough
planet heating emissions that they rival the emissions of Denmark. That's according to a
new study out in Nature. Here's NPR's Julia Simon.
The study looked at about 400 large U.S. data centers and estimated their electricity
consumption and carbon dioxide emissions. The team, led by researchers at Harvard University,
found the nation's largest data centers used about 2 percent of the country's electricity,
more than Los Angeles and New York combined. Most of the electricity for data centers came
from fossil fuels like natural gas and coal. Data center growth is one reason that U.S. greenhouse
gas emissions rose last year. According to a recent U.N. report, the U.S. sticks out as the
only major economy where planet warming pollution increased dramatically last year. Julia Simon,
NPR News. The Supreme Court has rejected a Trump administration appeal on DEI funding cuts to
academic research. That leaves in place lower court rulings. The administration likely violated
First Amendment rights by terminating millions of dollars in grants to University of California
researchers linked to diversity, equity and inclusion policies. Major U.S. stock indexes
fell today. This is NPR News. A Massachusetts judge has scheduled Lindsay Clancy's second trial
in the killings of her three children for late March. Clancy is charged with first-degree murder.
She has never disputed killing her children at the family's home in January 2023.
Her first trial ended in a mistrial after jurors deadlocked on whether she was criminally
responsible for the killings. The next James Bond has been announced. NPR's Jennifer Vinasco reports
the role of the suave British spy is going to a familiar front-runner. The British actor
Robert Pattinson will be the seventh James Bond, joining a list of stars that started with Sean
Connery and most recently included Daniel Craig. He was widely considered to be a finalist in the
casting race. Pattinson is known for big movies. He was Batman four years ago, a vampire in the
Twilight saga, and one of Penelope's suitors in this summer's hit The Odyssey. In a statement,
he called Bond a "legendary character." The next Bond movie will be directed by Dunes Denis Villeneuve.
Its release date has not yet been announced. Jennifer Vinasco, NPR News.
South Korean officials are scrambling to prevent the use of technology to cheat on a national
college entrance exam. More than 500,000 students nationwide will take the test on Thursday.
Concerns have grown that AI is making fraud harder to detect on the exam.
The top scorer on a national tax accountant exam has confessed to using a hidden micro camera
and smartphone to get answers from AI during the tests in April and July. I'm Rylan Barton.
